📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The second of Walmart's three major sales for Black Friday and Cyber Monday is now live, and there are some amazing tech deals to take advantage of. I've gathered my top 10 tech products from the sale below. For more, keep tabs on our Black Friday coverage, where we post the latest deals from not just Walmart, but Amazon, Best Buy, and other retailers' Black Friday sales.

In a recent development, apple's latest smartwatch is the Series 12, but don't count out the Series 11. By sacrificing a few of Apple's newest features, you can save some money on the more premium version of this last-gen Apple Watch. Right now, the Titanium Series 11 GPS + cellular model is on sale for $489.30 (originally $699).

It has been revealed that during WWDC 26 earlier this summer, Apple unveiled new Siri AI upgrades with watchOS 27—but only some Apple Watches have compatibility. Luckily, the Series 11 is one of them, at least for many of them. Some other upgrades in the new OS include a dedicated Siri app, a new app grid, a new single-tap gesture, among other features. Just note that only Series 12 and Ultra 4 can run Audio Intelligence.

The Garmin vivoactive 5 was $299.99 when it first came out in 2023 as their midrange lifestyle-focused fitness smartwatch. It features a 1.2-inch AMOLED touchscreen and an 11-day battery life (four to five days with the always-on display setting). You can get it for $169.99 right now. It's a great option for anyone looking to get into Garmin for the first time or upgrading from anything below it.

Bone conduction headphones are ideal for activities where it is vital to be able to hear your surroundings. They use a technology that sends audio vibrations to your inner ear while leaving your ear canals open. Shokz is one of, if not the best, brands making bone conduction headphones right now. At the high end of Shokz's offerings sit the OpenRun Pro 2, which impressed me when I tested them out for review. Walmart presently has a restored pair for $93 (originally $179.99 latest).

The latest AirPods Pro are a substantial step up. The third iteration of Apple's iconic earbuds comes with a number of quality-of-life and software improvements that make them worth the typical premium over the AirPods Pro 2—and right now, the AirPods Pro 3 are even cheaper than the previous generation. They're $149 on Walmart as an Black Friday deal, down from $249 and matching their lowest price ever.

Recent findings suggest that most, if not all, TV speakers aren't great. While you have plenty of options, the quickest and least expensive way to improve your TV's audio capabilities is to buy a soundbar. Compare a soundbar's size to the thin, small speakers jammed into modern TVs. The Vizio 5.1 Pro Soundbar with a subwoofer and rear speakers supports Dolby Atmos and costs just $99 (originally $198). They won't win any audio awards, but it's better than any built-in TV speakers, and for $99, it'll improve your experience without breaking the bank.

It has been revealed that if you want to take things up a notch, consider this 5.1 channel sound system. While it's a 5.1 system as well, it reaches a 312W peak power, which will make explosions and thuds feel more realistic. There's also a dedicated dialogue feature for people who don't like using subtitles. For $149.99 (originally $249.99), you can get the ULTIMEA 5.1 surround sound system.

It has been revealed that I love projectors and Roku. To me, a Roku projector just makes sense, especially at $119.99 (originally $389.99). This projector is portable and has the Roku OS already installed, so it's easy to project it against a wall, ceiling, or screen, whether it's indoors or outdoors. It's easy to set up; you just need an outlet nearby and to dim or turn off the lights. If you have Bluetooth speakers, you can hook them up to create a more immersive sound.

According to recent reports, the TCL Q51GB is a QLED Google TV that is a great value for anyone looking for size, color, and features. The 98-inch class is heavily discounted at its $898 price (originally $1,499.99). TCL makes one of the best QLEDs for the money, and their technology keeps getting better. This TV supports Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, and if you're a gamer, you get a refresh rate of 240Hz that is automatically triggered with its Auto Game Mode feature.

According to recent reports, if you've been holding off on buying a Nintendo Switch 2 until it went on sale and better games were available, now might be the time to pull the trigger. Right now, Walmart is offering the Mario World bundle for $499 (originally $549). The timing of this deal is even more noteworthy, given that Nintendo recently released the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

Industry observers note that gaming monitors can get pricey fast. At $159.99 (originally $299.99 at launch), this 27-inch Samsung Odyssey G55C curved gaming monitor offers a 1440p resolution, a 1000R curve, a 165Hz refresh rate with FreeSync and G-SYNC compatibility to keep screen tearing to a minimum, and features like Samsung’s Virtual Aim Point and Contrast Enhancer. It's a solid choice for gaming, especially at this price point.

Industry observers note that alienware makes great gaming laptops, and the Aurora is a great option for anyone who wants to get all the essentials without spending too much. At its current $1,099 price (originally $1,999), the Alienware Aurora 16 becomes a mid-tier gaming laptop at a "budget" price. We reviewed the higher-tier Aurora 16X and were impressed with it. The Aurora 16 has a slightly slower processor, a dimmer display with half the refresh rate, a smaller battery, and a weaker graphics card, but given its price, it's great for a gamer looking for a solid gaming laptop in the $1,000 range.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Amazon has a much larger inventory of tech products on sale, but the ones they both sell are mostly priced the same. While Amazon may have more deals, Walmart usually has a couple of surprise flagship tech products on sale that Amazon will later price match. So taking all of that into consideration, the best one will be whichever has whatever you're looking to buy at the lower price.

According to recent reports, yes. I own these headphones and can vouch they are worth every penny. The headphones are high quality and bring a hybrid style of open earbuds and bone conduction that I haven't seen in other headphones.

Should you buy the Amazon Kids Kindle or a standard Paperwhite for your child? Here’s what’s different

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1000 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There comes a point when your child is old enough to potentially get their own Kindle, mostly so they stop stealing yours and filling up your library with Significant Nate collections.
  • Now is the perfect time to find the right Kindle for your child, as Amazon typically puts many of its Kindles on sale for Black Friday.
  • In a recent development, unfortunately, none of them are on sale, and in general they're more expensive than their "adult" counterparts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There comes a point when your child is old enough to potentially get their own Kindle, mostly so they stop stealing yours and filling up your library with Significant Nate collections.

Now is the perfect time to find the right Kindle for your child, as Amazon typically puts many of its Kindles on sale for Black Friday. You may not have known that Amazon has kid versions of the Kindle, Paperwhite and Colorsoft.

In a recent development, unfortunately, none of them are on sale, and in general they're more expensive than their "adult" counterparts. But Amazon also offers a bit more out of the box with the kid versions.

Let's break down what you get with the Kid Kindle and why the higher price may be worth it.

To be up front, as far as we can tell, the different Kindle Kids eReaders are the same hardware that you get with the standard Kindle, Paperwhite and Colorsoft.

Industry observers note that the difference is that the Kid version comes with a case included. Right now, the Paperwhite Kids can be purchased with the Pirate theme, "Bookman," or Lakeside Retreat.

Sources indicate that additionally, the Kid Kindles come with a 1-year Kids+ subscription included. Basically, this is a more curated version of Kindle Plus (the rebranded of Kindle Unlimited) for children. It includes thousands of books for kids ages 6 through 12, like the Percy Jackson series or Diary of a Wimpy Kid. Also, the Kid version does not come with ads or distractions.

The Kid Kindles also have parent controls that can be accessed through the Parent Dashboard mobile app which can be used to suggest books or set screen limits.

It has been revealed that amazon updated most of its Kindle lineup earlier this year, but the 2024 version of the Kindle Paperwhite Kids is still available and the only Kids eReader on sale at $149. This version comes with 16GB of storage, a case, 6 months of Amazon Kids+, and a waterproof design.

By comparison, the adult Kindles do not come with a case, only three months of Kindle+ (which adds a cost), and you have to choose ad-supported or without lockscreen ads (again more expensive).

There are content controls and parent controls on normal Kindles, but in my experience, it's more finicky and usually requires a separate account if you truly want to lock things down. Quite annoying when you're sharing with your child and your wife is filling the library with romantasy novels. Not yet, buddy, not yet.

Both the kids and adult versions can be used to access library books through the Libby app, literally the best thing about Kindles compared to most other eReaders.

Here's the massive difference: price. Let's use the Kindle Paperwhite as our example.

The Ad-free, 3-month Kindle+, Paperwhite costs $219 when its not on sale. The ad-supported version costs $199. The newly introduced Kids Kindle Paperwhite costs $229.

For a less expensive option, the cheapest standard Kindle is $149, while the Kids version costs $179. The case adds up the Kids version, but if you want a case for the adult version, the cheapest one I saw on Amazon tacks on $21 to the price.

According to recent reports, if money isn't as big of a concern, the Kids Kindle Colorsoft is $299 but is great for kids who starting to read comic books or if you want the option for color stories. The base adult Colorsoft starts at $289 but there is a bundle with a case for $301, which is on sale.

Amazon refreshed the Kids Kindle this year with a thinner and lighter version. It features a 6-inch glare-free display, a themed case, and 1-year of Kids+ subscription. The Kids Kindle has up to 6 weeks of battery life and you can listen to audio books using Bluetooth headphones. Parents can control settings with the Parent dashboard.

The big difference is that I rarely see the Kid versions go on sale while the standard Kindles get discounted throughout the year typically around Black Friday, the new Spring sale and the big Prime Day summer sale.

In a recent development, also, the subscription. You get three months of Kindle+ which normally costs $11.99 per month (or $143.88) for a year. The Kid Kindle comes with 12 months of Kids+, which normally costs $7.99 a month for Prime Members or $8.99 if you don't have an account.

Additionally, if you have other Amazon devices like the Amazon Kids Echo or an Amazon Kids tablet, your Kids+ subscription is accessible across each device with a child profile.

The upfront costs of the Kid Kindle is higher in general, but over the first year, if you keep the subscription, you're paying on par with the adult Kindle and getting more control and curation.

As we noted above, you don't have to get the newest model and Amazon has done a decent job of supporting much older Kindles.

In this case, don't let the sticker shock get to you and consider the Kindle Kid, Kindle Paperwhite Kid, or Kindle Colorsoft Kid for your child.

Denver man traps Waymo robotaxis with cones, eggs them at least 30 times

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A man in Denver has found a cheap way to beat Waymo’s self-driving system: a few orange traffic cones and a carton of eggs.
  • Industry observers note that waymo says it has counted at least 30 egg attacks on its robotaxis in Denver, all believed to be the same man.
  • The method is laid out in a Denver police report filed last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A man in Denver has found a cheap way to beat Waymo’s self-driving system: a few orange traffic cones and a carton of eggs.

Industry observers note that waymo says it has counted at least 30 egg attacks on its robotaxis in Denver, all believed to be the same man. And the Denver District Attorney’s Office has declined to file charges, calling it a civil matter, according to The Fresh York Times.

The method is laid out in a Denver police report filed last month. The man pulls up in front of a Waymo somewhere in or around downtown, takes orange cones out of his trunk, and sets them around the robotaxi so it can’t drive off. Then come the eggs, sometimes thrown from his driver’s seat, sometimes after he gets out.

Industry observers note that he leaves in a silver Toyota Corolla. Per the report, that car belongs to a fleet leased out to Lyft drivers. The man hasn’t been identified, and Lyft didn’t comment.

A Waymo investigator took seven of the incidents to police. Each egged vehicle had to come out of service for cleaning, and the detailing bill came to about $2,000. No permanent damage.

Police brought their findings to prosecutors, who decided “no criminal charges” were appropriate. A spokesperson for the DA told the Times the office is now collecting evidence on potential damage and will work with the city attorney to find “the most appropriate legal mechanism to make this behavior stop.”.

Recent findings suggest that at least one Waymo had a rider inside. Jeff Hunley was headed to the Union Station neighborhood in September when his robotaxi got hit. He filmed it, said he felt safe in the car, and got his fare refunded.

Waymo opened its Denver service to the public on September 1, alongside San Diego and Tampa. The organization now runs more than 100 vehicles across 60 square miles of the city, and Mayor Mike Johnston is a fan. He called them popular and affordable, and couldn’t resist adding that “overall they’re a good egg.”.

Recent findings suggest that the rest of November hasn’t been as friendly. California’s DMV ordered Waymo’s driverless vehicles off state freeways on November 11 after robotaxis drove into active construction zones and one tried to get past a CHP traffic break. Waymo responded by pausing freeway rides in every US market.

And vandalism isn’t new for Waymo. We covered it when at least five of its I-Pace robotaxis were set on fire during protests in Los Angeles last year.

Putting a single cone on a Waymo’s hood to freeze it has been a known trick since San Francisco activists did it in 2023. Ringing the car with cones works for the same reason: the Waymo Driver is built to respect them, and it won’t push through.

Sources indicate that A human driver getting pelted with eggs would just roll over a cone and leave. A robotaxi sits there and takes it.

That’s the correct default. You don’t want a driverless car deciding when a cone is optional, especially two weeks after regulators pulled Waymo off California freeways for ignoring work zones. But it means anyone with a trunk full of cones can pin a robotaxi in place for as long as they want.

In a recent development, we’ll try to keep the egg puns to a minimum. Mostly.

It has been revealed that can't help but respect the guy's dedication? This guy is causing road hazards by his childish shenanigans. There is nothing to respect about this guy. I never understood why anyone would support people that hinder technological progress that ultimately makes it safer for pedestrians, cyclists and other drivers. The more human drivers we get off the road the safer we all are.

Sources indicate that this is small-time vandalism. Two grand in cleaning, no injuries, no lasting damage. But it shows a real weakness in robotaxis: they’re designed to be the most cautious car on the road, and a determined person can turn that caution against them in under a minute. The car can’t escape, can’t honk its way out, and apparently can’t stop the same guy from coming back 30 times.

The DA’s call is hard to follow. Prosecutors have a repeat pattern, a vehicle tied to a known fleet operator, rider video, and robotaxis that are basically rolling camera rigs. And still no charges. If someone boxed in a regular taxi with a passenger inside and started throwing things at it, we suspect the answer would be different.

At the same time, I can’t help but respect the guy’s dedication.

Jalen Brunson might be a pro at scoring baskets for the New York Knicks, but now the NBA champ is helping shoppers score a different kind of win with Lowe’s Black Friday deals.

The superstar has teamed up with the home improvement retailer as an ambassador for its Black Friday campaign, which features hundreds of discounts on everything from tools to holiday decor and kitchen essentials. Better yet, Lowe’s is hosting a massive giveaway for shoppers willing to brave the crowds on the 27th.

It has been revealed that the first 50 people (starting at 6 a.m. local time) to enter a participating store will receive a “Free Lowe’s Black Friday Mystery Bucket” filled with more than 10 goodies and special surprises, per the brand. And because this is the season of giving, there are even more bargains awaiting early shoppers. According to the tech giant, “four of the first 50 members at every Lowe’s store will win one of the day’s top prizes.” This includes:.

While this may be Brunson’s latest endeavor, the baller has kept busy on all fronts. Between appearing on SNL, making a cameo on Law & Order: SVU, and kicking off a new NBA season, he’s been making the rounds both on and off the court. It’s also far from his first brand partnership. He first teamed up with Lowe’s back in May and has since worked with several other companies, including Nike, Faherty, and Lingua Franca.

Recent findings suggest that we spoke with Brunson about his partnership with Lowe’s, his status as a loud and proud Belieber, and his favorite family holiday traditions. Read the full interview below and shop our other favorite Black Friday deals now.

Why did Lowe’s feel like a natural partner to you?I feel like we embody a lot of the same qualities. One thing I grew up learning was the importance of serving others and helping people, and I feel like Lowe’s shares that same commitment. Our priorities align, so it felt natural to work with them.

Sources indicate that do you have any holiday traditions that are non-negotiable for you and your family?The only real non-negotiable is that we’re together. One thing I really love that my family does is keep an open house for people I work with, especially those who aren’t from New York or have family far away. We’re always happy to welcome anyone who needs a Thanksgiving or Christmas meal. Whoever wants to join us is welcome.

According to recent reports, new York Knicks fans are famously passionate. Is there something about the city or its fans that still surprises you?Nothing surprises me anymore. The fans are going to be who they are. They’re unapologetic, they’re vocal, and they’re going to let you know when you’re playing great and when you’re playing bad. That’s just who they are, and it’s something I’ve grown to love. I wouldn’t want it any other way. They set a certain level of expectation for us, and we have to live up to it. They know we’re capable of it. That’s why they push us.

Is there a particular fan moment that sticks out to you, or do you tend to lump them all together?I put them all together, but the parade was absolutely absurd. There are some things I probably can’t talk about, but I saw a lot during the parade. The fans had been waiting for that for a long time, so they deserved to let loose and enjoy it.

Industry observers note that when you’re warming up before a game, what’s on your playlist? What gets you in the zone?It depends on the day. My music taste is all over the place, but one thing that’s become a superstition for me is that the last song I listen to in my headphones has to be a Bieber song.

Do you have a favorite Bieber song, or is it truly just anything?“Organization” is one of my favorite songs, but honestly, it could be anything.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic is launching a upcoming tool for builders called Claude Ship. The new AI feature allows Claude to “review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows.”.

Industry observers note that claude Ship is a newly introduced product created especially for builders who code with agents. The idea is to make handling pull requests as automated as agentic coding.

“That’s why we built Claude Ship, available today in beta,” Anthropic states. “It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what’s ready to merge based on policies each team sets. Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person. The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

Claude Ship is comprised of three agents: Code Review, PR Steward, and Claude Approvals.

“Together, they take a pull request through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually,” Anthropic says.

“Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the upcoming /ship command in Claude Code,” Anthropic notes.

You can learn much more about Claude Ship here. Additional documentation can be found here.

Donald Trump celebrated Thanksgiving by posting a lengthy screed taking aim at the “radical far left,” critics of his ballroom project, and “murderers, drug dealers, and criminals of all shapes, sizes, and colors.”.

The president, writing on Truth Social, opened the post with a sincere note: “HAPPY THANKSGIVING TO ALL AMERICAN PATRIOTS WHO HAVE WORKED SO HARD TO MAKE OUR COUNTRY GREAT!” He then introduced into a rant-filled tirade that was far less grateful.

“Additionally, I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%, A RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated,” Trump wrote. “Also, I would like to wish a very Happy Thanksgiving to all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left, those that are looking to change our Court System to that of Sharia, those who want to redistribute Property, so that all of the hardworking people that have built up, over a lifetime, a certain Wealth, will now be forced to distribute it throughout the Country, even to those who refuse to work.”.

Industry observers note that he continued, “I want to thank the 2% of our Somalian population that have a job, and are actually willing to work, without receiving Government Assistance. These are wonderful American ‘citizens,’ and should be allowed to stay in our Country, and celebrate Thanksgiving with us. The others should be thrown out, immediately, thereby saving the Great State of Minnesota, which has no chance if they are allowed to stay.”.

He then shifted focus to the White House and his ballroom, which has yet to be completed. “I want to commiserate with those Reporters and Citizens who don’t understand filth, dirt, lack of maintenance, and corruption, and are upset with me because I took time out of my very busy schedule to fix the 17 broken windows, numerous chipped and decaying columns, broken, dilapidated, and missing moldings, and lack of a proper plaster and paint job on the White House,” Trump noted. “It hasn’t been properly painted, or taken care of, for years. I felt strongly that, after being built in 1792, it was time to fix up the White House which is, after all, a primary symbol of our Country. Today, it has never looked better, and will soon have the Ballroom that Presidents have sought for over 150 years.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

He concluded with a final thank you to “the murderers, drug dealers, and criminals of all shapes, sizes, and colors, who illegally entered our Country from other countries’ jails, prisons, mental institutions, and places unknown, to rape, plunder, and kill American Citizens in record numbers.”.

Sources indicate that “They are mostly gone now, brought back to their point of origin and, hopefully, living a beautiful and idyllic life, and promising, ideally, never to kill innocent people again, but we won’t have to worry about that, because they are GONE but, Happy Thanksgiving to them anyway, even though from Faraway Lands,” Trump affirmed. “We miss you dearly, but you will never be back, and America will never allow what you have done to us to happen again!” Trending Stories Duran Duran Guitarist Andy Taylor Dead at 65 U2 Perform Dolly Parton's Final Recording During NFL Halftime Show ⁠Gérard Depardieu to Face Trial for Allegedly Raping Actress Charlotte ⁠Arnould Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor Was the Wildest of the Wild Boys.

This webinar will demonstrate how the COMSOL Multiphysics software supports predictive modeling by coupling electromagnetic fields with thermal, chemical, mechanical, and transport phenomena across multiple length and time scales.The first application we will show focuses on eddy-current thermometry for reconstructing three-dimensional temperature fields in metal plates. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's no better time to buy a Garmin watch than the Black Friday sales, because it's almost always the period you'll find the lowest prices available on any Garmin.

This year the sale is especially good, because not only have excellent older Garmin watches like the Forerunner 265 and Forerunner 965 returned to their lowest-ever price, but the latest Garmin watches like the Fenix 9 and Forerunner 170 have also been significantly discounted for the first time.

I've been testing Garmin watches for a decade and I think the only watch I can't find a deal on right now is the Enduro 4, but even there you don't have to worry, because the almost equally good Enduro 3 is down to $699 at Amazon.

I’ve picked out 17 deals on the best Garmin watches available right now, from cheaper Forerunner models all the way up to the Garmin Fenix 8 Pro, which is $849 in the Amazon sale and still a better buy than the Fenix 9 in the sale, in my opinion.

I think the Forerunner 70 is the best beginner running watch available, and it actually has all the features runners of all levels really need. It's accurate and comfortable to wear 24/7 thanks to its small design, and this is the first time it's dropped under $200 on sale.

The Forerunner 165 is the predecessor to the Forerunner 70 and Forerunner 170 watches, and a good pick, especially for new runners. This is one of the few Garmin deals I'm a little disappointed by this Black Friday, though, because the Forerunner 165 has dropped as low as $129 in the past.

According to recent reports, the Forerunner 170 has a few extra features compared to the Forerunner 70, most notably music storage, and also comes in this delightful teal color ( which I'd say makes it worth the upgrade alone). It's a great running watch and is getting its first big discounts this Black Friday.

This is the biggest percentage discount I've seen on a Garmin watch right now, and it makes the Instinct 3 AMOLED a strong, adventurous alternative to the Fenix and Enduro. It offers incredible battery life and a distinctive, rugged design, as well as reliable sports tracking, but it does lack the maps you get on pricier models.

This is one of the best deals going on for a Garmin right now, because even though the Forerunner 265 is an older watch, it's still an excellent multisport tracker with a bright AMOLED display. It even comes in two sizes and I'd say the only watch that can rival it for this price is the Coros Pace 4.

The Vivoactive 6 is an attractive smartwatch with impressive sports tracking credentials. It has dropped as low as $229 in the past, so a better deal might be yet to come on the watch this Black Friday, but this is still a good price on a well-rounded watch.

According to recent reports, the Forerunner 965 is the best alternative to newer top models like the Forerunner 970 and even the Fenix lineup if you're looking for value this Black Friday. It has brilliant sports tracking and navigation features, and a thin, lightweight design. You'll be hard-pressed to find a better watch from any brand for $449.

The Garmin Venu 4 combines its attractive, smartwatch-style design with Garmin's excellent sports tracking, and even as a marathoner, I prefer it to the more sports-focused Forerunner 570, partly because it has a built-in flashlight.

I don't think the Forerunner 570 offers better value than the Venu 4 or Forerunner 965 at the same price, but it does have some more striking design options than those watches, which might tempt you ot pick it up instead. It's a great sports tracker, of course, but lacks maps and a flashlight.

In a recent development, the Venu X1 stands out from other Garmins thanks to its ultra-thin design, but even though it looks like a smartwatch, it's actually packed with the same brilliant sports and navigation features as you get on the Forerunner 970. At $300 off, it might be the sleeper hit of the sales.

The Epix Pro is the value alternative to the latest Fenix watches, but I'm a little disappointed it hasn't dropped to a lower price than this, because it has been as cheap as $499 in the past.

It has been revealed that I rate the Garmin Forerunner 970 as the best overall sports watch on the market, so getting any kind of discount on it is welcome, and this is a return to the lowest price it's ever been available. It has all of Garmin's top sports tracking and training analysis features, plus maps, all in a lightweight, durable design.

This is a good price for a great adventure watch if you prefer a MIP display, but the fact that the Fenix 7 Pro has been superseded by three rounds of Fenixes at this point makes me hope there might still be better deals to come. If not, this is still worth looking at as the cheapest titanium Garmin watch with maps and a MIP display on sale.

I've just tested the Garmin Enduro 4 and I'd say the Enduro 3 is the better value buy for sure, because it has all the same key features as the new watch for $200 less on sale. Those features include the longest battery life of any Garmin, thanks to the Enduro 4's MIP display and solar panels.

It has been revealed that the Fenix 8 has now been superseded by the Fenix 8 Pro and Fenix 9, but I think it's still worth considering because it's cheaper than those watches on sale. You don't get the connectivity features available on newer Fenixes, but otherwise the Fenix 8 matches up well with regard to its core features, and it's also a little thinner than the upcoming models.

The fresh Fenix 9 Pro has a few upgrades over the Fenix 8 Pro, including an all-titanium case, and is also on sale, but the Fenix 8 Pro is still a savvier buy thanks to this $350 saving, in my opinion. It has LTE and satellite connectivity on top of its outstanding sports tracking and navigation features, and is $150 less than the Fenix 9 Pro right now on sale.

Recent findings suggest that all models of the Garmin Fenix 9 are reduced by at least $100 for Black Friday, including the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro with InReach, which is the watch I'm using as my main tracker right now. If you want the latest and greatest Garmin watch, this is the time to buy it, because it's the first time it's been discounted anywhere.

Nick Harris-Fry is an experienced health and fitness journalist, writing professionally since 2012. Nick is a keen runner and also the founder of YouTube channel The Run Testers, which specialises in reviewing running shoes, watches, headphones and other gear.

The Kodak SlideTag is inspired by classic 35mm slides from Kodak cameras, and is built by the same tech giant, Reto, that rolled out a keychain digital camera inspired by old Kodak cameras too. The tracker’s E-Ink display is designed mainly to showcase your photos, with storage built-in for up to 12 photos, but also the ability to show lists and QR codes.

3 tips for shopping for a mattress for back pain in the Black Friday sales.

I've had recurrent lower back pain for over a decade, so I know how much it can impact your ability to stay asleep all night. If you are a shopping for a mattress for back pain in the Black Friday sales, there's a few things to keep in mind. 1. Choose a mattress with lumbar support Your lumbar region is the curve at your lower back. A mattress with enhanced lumbar support will support this natural ‘S’ shape, comfortably filling this gap and distributing your weight evenly. The Saatva RX, Saatva Classic and Helix Midnight Luxe are just a handful of mattresses that support the lumbar beautifully. 2. Opt for the right firmness It’s a common misconception that when it comes to back pain, the firmer the mattress the better. Instead, most chiropractors recommend a medium-firm mattress as the sweet spot between pressure relief and support. However, those who weigh over 230lb or are back or stomach sleepers might find relief from a firmer mattress. Check out our guide on how to choose a mattress for more advice on mattress firmness.

In a recent development, 3. Make sure it comes with a sleep trialSometimes the mattress you buy ticks all the right boxes on paper, but doesn’t quite meet your sleep needs. That’s why I always recommend buying a mattress with a sleep trial. Sleep trials usually range between 90 and 365 nights, and is the window of time you return your mattress if it isn’t quite right.Read more: We tested back pain mattresses from Helix, Saatva, Plank and Brooklyn Bedding — these are the deals we recommend and how to choose between these beds this Black Friday.

Should you buy a mattress from Amazon this Black Friday?

According to recent reports, you can buy anything at Amazon, even a upcoming mattress — but should you? I'm going to have a quick scout around to see if any new deals have dropped at Amazon overnight. In the meantime, check out my pros and cons of buying a new mattress from the online marketplace below.

✅Cheap deals: You can often pay less for a mattress on Amazon than if you were to buy it directly from the brand, even if it is only on certain sizes.

Recent findings suggest that ✅Faster shipping: The Black Friday sales can cause an increase in demand, leading to shipping delays and back orders. Amazon, on the other hand, is known for their speedy delivery — a huge plus if you need a bed before Christmas.

According to recent reports, ✅More options: Brands run out of stock or discontinue certain models when revamping their collections. Amazon gives you the chance to buy discontinued models and items that are sold out on the brand’s website.

Recent findings suggest that ❌No guaranteed sleep trials or warranties: The beauty of buying directly from a brand is that their benefits are clearly outlined, such as a sleep trial. While Amazon usually offers 90-100 day returns, they don’t offer official trials which allow you to sleep on your purchase for an allotted number of weeks to see if it's right for you.

❌Less reputable: While you can find mattresses and bed toppers from trusted brands at Amazon, there are a lot of cheaper beds from less well known brands that you may be tempted by, but aren’t always the best quality.

What do we know about mattresses?

Recent findings suggest that why can you trust us to guide you towards the right mattress for you? Collectively, our team has clocked up over 24,000 hours testing mattresses. We approach mattress testing from two distinct viewpoints; what does it feel like to sleep on night after night? And how does it perform during our objective tests? In addition to sleeping on it for a minimum of three weeks, during which time we invite friends and family members to offer their feedback, we conduct a series of tests in sleep studio lab. Here, we test against motion isolation, temperature control and pressure relief. You can find out more about how we test mattresses in our mattress methodology.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iconic YouTube app icon that looked like a retro TV found on iOS might be making a comeback, with new customizable icons showing up behind the scenes of a new YouTube update.

According to recent reports, in the early days of the iPhone, Apple built a custom app for YouTube on iOS before Google built its own. That included an app icon that looked like a retro TV and it was later replaced when YouTube’s official app launched on the platform.

Now, that icon might be coming back.

Android Authority spotted several newly introduced app icons YouTube for Android is testing in its latest beta revision (v21.47.483-BETA). These icons seem to be tied to a new feature that would allow users to customize the homescreen icon for YouTube, and includes seven designs in total including two throwback designs. One is the aforementioned retro TV icon used on iOS, which was never on YouTube for Android, and another is an old stacked YouTube logo design.

That mentioned, it’s very fun to get these throwbacks, and we’ll be excited to see this functionality go live.

Ariana Grande’s Best On-Screen Roles

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that ariana Grande may be one of the biggest pop stars in the world, but she’s also a true multi-hyphenate, known for her uncanny impressions and acting chops.
  • It has been revealed that now, she’s starring alongside Robert De Niro in the new movie Focker-In-Law, which is out this week.
  • Part of what makes Grande’s acting career so much fun to watch is that she never does what anyone is expecting her to do — and she’s not above extreme silliness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that ariana Grande may be one of the biggest pop stars in the world, but she’s also a true multi-hyphenate, known for her uncanny impressions and acting chops. Grande can hit a killer vocal run, produce a sleek beat, and steal a scene with terrific comedic timing. (It’s called range.) Her Hollywood career has grown with her pop star status — she started as a Broadway baby, singing her heart out in the musical 13, and eventually became one of Nickelodeon’s most beloved airheads as she played Cat Valentine on Victorious.

It has been revealed that now, she’s starring alongside Robert De Niro in the new movie Focker-In-Law, which is out this week. So what better time to look back at the roles that have helped the megastar get to this point? Here are some of her most impressive moments both on the substantial and small screens.

Part of what makes Grande’s acting career so much fun to watch is that she never does what anyone is expecting her to do — and she’s not above extreme silliness. That makes her Zoolander 2 performance particularly entertaining. It’s extremely brief, but she pops on-screen just in time to have a wild orgy with Hansel (Owen Wilson). The scene marked her first time meeting Ben Stiller, who she reunites with in Focker-In-Law. She looked back at their meet-cute fondly during a recent appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon: “He was directing me in an orgy scene in Zoolander 2 with a hippo and Susan Sarandon,” she shared. “So right off the bat, we had a comfortability.” —Julyssa Lopez.

Grande is one of the best parts of Adam McKay’s 2021 satire Don’t Look Up. She plays Riley Bina, a major pop star who is out-of-touch with the world — and the fact that a humanity-ending comet is headed Earth’s way. Once people start believing PhD student Kate Dibiasky (Jennifer Lawrence) and her advisor Dr. Randall Mindy (Leonardo DiCaprio) about their chilling prediction, Bina performs her upcoming song “Just Look Up” with her cheating boyfriend, DJ Chello (Kid Cudi). The scene finds Grande delivering killer one-liners like, “Listen to the goddamn qualified scientists, we really fucked it up this time” while suspended onstage and sporting a ridiculous get-up of white feathers. According to McKay, many of the song’s lyrics were improvised by Grande. —Maya Georgi.

In 2013, Nickelodeon adapted Gordon Korman’s 2008 novel Swindle, shaping it into a made-for-television heist movie revolving around two friends who set out to recover a $1.2 million baseball card. They form an unlikely group with other kids from their school harboring secret skills, and Grande steps in as a cheerleader with an undercover geeky side. The film came during her Sam & Cat days, and teamed her up with co-star Jennette McCurdy, while also letting her go beyond her flaky Cat persona. —J.L.

When Grande reprises the role of Glinda for the second half of the Wicked tale, she’s planning her wedding to Prince Fiyero, all of Emerald City idolizes her, and everything is as she always wished — or is it? As Glinda reevaluates her life and decides to change paths to help her friend Elphaba (Cynthia Erivo), there are fewer of the rollicking comedy moments that made Grande’s performance in the first film so fun to watch. But with big songs like “I Couldn’t Be Happier,” “The Girl in the Bubble,” and the booming duet “For Good,” she makes clear why she was a natural fit for the iconic role. —Kate Storey.

According to recent reports, guest-starring on the campy horror-comedy television show Scream Queens as Chanel #2 was Ariana Grande’s first adult role after leaving Nickelodeon’s Sam & Cat to focus on her music. Creator Ryan Murphy mentioned in 2015 that initially, Grande “was just going to do one episode, but she loved the process so much that she wanted to do more.” Even though she played a corpse in a few of those episodes, Ari’s comedic skills shine through, especially in a scene where her character’s ghost visits Emma Roberts’ Chanel #1. Grande is hilarious when speaking about her afterlife in hell. Whether her character is that she’s in a bad mood because Adolf Hitler was motorboating her boobs or that Jesus broke into heaven and stole the dinosaurs, she steals every scene. —Alison Weinflash.

Industry observers note that let’s look beyond the fact that Cat Valentine seemingly has a legitimate lobotomy in the middle of the Victorious run. There would not be an Ariana Grande without the exposure, preparation, and genuine war stories that the cast ofVictorious went through. While the will-they-won’t-they nature of Cat’s relationship with Robbie (Matt Bennett) was finally resolved in the apocalyptic music video for “One Last Time,” the most memorable musical moments of the series all involved Grande: from the karaoke bar rendition of “Give it Up” to the “They didn’t say I couldn’t sing” riff on the Victorious iCarly collab “Leave It All to Shine.” As Cat, Grande earned her place in the Hollywood Arts High School hall of fame and started her path toward becoming a household name. —C.T. Jones.

Sources indicate that ariana Grande has hosted SNL three times now, and she always makes her appearances memorable by leveraging her exceptional impersonation skills, showcasing her comedy agility, and refusing to shy away from being wildly silly. We’ve seen her play Jennifer Lawrence during a Family Feud recreation and playing a shy intern who saves her radio station with her ability to sound like everyone from Shakira to Celine Dion. But her most beloved contributions might be in an off-key bridesmaid in the famed Domingo skit and giving us a hilarious take on Home Alone. —J.L.

Sources indicate that grande’s character in Focker In Law, Olivia Jones, is a multi-hyphenate not unlike the actress who portrays her. Just swap the gold records for FBI credentials, throw in vegan cooking chops, and you have a future in-law (to grandpa Jack Byrnes, reprised brilliantly by Robert De Niro) hell-bent on entering the “circle of trust” in record time. Grande plays the ultra-competitive Liv with exacting comedic timing, offering the perfect foil for Ben Stiller’s goofball insecurity. —Shirley Halperin.

It takes self-determination, drive, and a lot of pink to make the world’s most coveted role your own. Ariana Grande wasn’t the frontrunner when Universal first unveiled it would be making a Wicked film. But the Petal singer fought to claim Glinda’s glitter wand. “Oz has been my safe space for as long as I can remember,” she wrote in an open letter to fans before the film’s premiere. It’s hard to imagine a world where the gleeful shrieks of Grande’s “Popular” outro didn’t exist — and her participation in the John M. Chu duology is a career-defining moment, proof the former Nick star is never far from her musical theater roots. —C.T.J.

Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a fresh e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a substantial discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is at the moment 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Sources indicate that xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink quickly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

It has been revealed that the X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

It has been revealed that these upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 released at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also important to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing fresh firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

Apple Photos got a lot of latest features in iOS 27, but the recent release of iOS 27.2 brought even more improvements. Here’s what’s new.

Recent findings suggest that shared Albums are among my favorite features in the Photos app. I don’t post on social media often, but I love using Shared Albums because they provide a social media-style experience in a private way that lives right inside Photos.

iOS 27 brought a variety of big improvements to Shared Albums. And in iOS 27.2, Apple introduced four more.

Per Apple’s release notes, here’s what’s latest:.

To get these newly introduced features, you’ll need to make sure your Shared Albums have been upgraded for iOS 27.

One complication introduced by AI is that it can be hard to know if an image is real or AI-generated.

This challenge extends to AI-edited photos too, which might have key details changed by tools like iOS 27’s Extend, Reframe, and Clean Up features in Photos.

Apple is tackling the matter with its newly introduced Reference Image feature in iPhone 18 Pro, and also through a software enhancement that rolled out in iOS 27.2.

Per Apple, its latest software update adds the following:.

Support for SynthID watermarking to help identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground.

SynthID is a cross-platform standard developed by Google that embeds unnoticeable digital watermarks into AI-modified photos. Customers won’t see a visible watermark, but anyone who checks for a SynthID marker will find it.

#143986. What’s the difference between an automatic and manual espresso machine — and the one an ex-barista recommends

What’s the difference between an automatic and manual espresso machine — and the one an ex-barista recommends

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1537 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coffee can feel like an overwhelming pastime.
  • But the most important difference is the type of espresso machine you buy.
  • Industry observers note that what type of espresso machine is best for you, and which should you buy?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coffee can feel like an overwhelming pastime. There's so much noise online about coffee — grind size, flow rate, milk texture — that I'm surprised any newbies are brave enough to take the plunge and buy their first espresso machine.

But the most important difference is the type of espresso machine you buy. There are loads of different types of machines for different types of coffee drinkers: superautomatic, semi-automatic, manual, bean-to-cup/all-in-one... the list goes on. Today, let's get to the bottom of it.

Industry observers note that what type of espresso machine is best for you, and which should you buy? I'm using Casabrews, Ninja, and De'Longhi espresso machines to exemplify my points today — and they're all on sale for Black Friday.

The De'Longhi Rivelia is my favorite automatic espresso machine. It has two hoppers so you can switch out beans if you so please, and it makes both hot and cold drinks at the push of a button (but you have to buy the cold frother separately, unfortunately).

It has been revealed that the Casabrews 3700 Essential is the best espresso machine under $100 (of the ones I've tested). This machine makes delicious coffee, and while you need to spend a little time learning how to use it, it's totally worth it.

According to recent reports, the Ninja Luxe Cafe Mini Plus is like the best of all worlds. It has a built-in grinder and tamping assist to prevent messes, and it has both manual and automatic milk frothing. This machine is great for learning how to be a barista.

There's one key difference between automatic and manual machines: ease of use. (Size and price also come into play!).

Automatic machines are called that for a reason: press a button, and you get hot coffee in seconds.

An automatic coffee machine selection screen generally looks something like this.

Recent findings suggest that some machines have upwards of 50 recipes. The De'Longhi PrimaDonna Aromatic ($2,499) offers 38 recipes — some of which I, an ex-barista, had never heard of — including hot and cold beverages. At the press of a button, the machine makes your drink for you.

Depending on price, some automatic machines have integrated milk frothing, like the pictured De'Longhi Rivelia ($1,499) or the De'Longhi Magnifica Duo ($999).

You don't have to do anything. No grinding, no tamping, no calculating dosage volume. As long as there are beans in the hopper, water in the tank, and electricity in the machine, it'll take care of everything.

In a recent development, automatic machines are ideal if you drink a lot of coffee, but either you don't have time to make it yourself, or you don't want to make it yourself. Both are valid.

But what about a manual espresso machine? Manual espresso machines vary in functionality — some have built-in grinders, so closer to automatics, but some are incredibly hands-on. Let's run through a few examples.

This is the Casabrews 3700 Essential. It's the cheapest espresso machine I've rated highly, and my only recommendation for a sub-$100 espresso machine. If you want the cheapest manual espresso machine on the market, I'd go for this one.

It has been revealed that this machine necessitates either a separate grinder or getting your coffee ground for espresso at a local cafe. It comes with dual-walled (pressurized) coffee baskets. While a pressurized basket means it doesn't make "technically" perfect espresso, it's a fantastic machine to learn on, as it's incredibly forgiving.

However, you do need to spend a bit of time learning the ropes. Unlike an automatic machine, you have to do everything yourself. You need to grind the coffee, put the coffee in the portafilter, press "start", and steam your milk.

If you want to get into coffee as a hobby, or you like the routine of making coffee, then I would recommend a manual machine such as this.

However, if you want to make your life easier and you have a little more money to spend, I'd also recommend looking at manual espresso machines with built-in grinders, like the Ninja Luxe Cafe Mini Plus.

According to recent reports, as you can see, this machine has a lot more going on than the Casabrews 3700 Essential. The Ninja Luxe Cafe Mini Plus has a built-in grinder (on the left) and tamping assist (also on the left).

Although you still need to put beans in the hopper and adjust grind size yourself, this machine takes a lot of the hassle out of your morning brew. The Luxe Cafe Mini doesn't have automatic milk frothing, but the Luxe Cafe Mini Plus (pictured) does. The Mini will set you back $449, while the Plus goes for $499. Right now, though, the Mini Plus is $419, and the Mini is $399.

Recent findings suggest that the long and short of it is this: No time to spend making coffee? Just want coffee, stat? Automatic — De'Longhi Rivelia.

Want to learn the art of coffee, and don't mind buying a grinder or getting your beans ground at a cafe? Manual — Casabrews 3700 Essential.

Sources indicate that still want to make the coffee yourself, but you want a built-in grinder? Manual with a built-in grinder — Ninja Luxe Cafe Mini Plus.

In a recent development, although not as integral as ease of use, size is also something to consider. In general, automatic machines are pretty huge. Here's a size comparison of our three case studies.

Ninja Luxe Cafe Mini Plus (manual, grinder).

Casabrews 3700 Essential (manual, no grinder).

According to recent reports, if you're short on space, the answer's kind of obvious — it should probably be a manual with no grinder. However, you need to remember you will either require a separate grinder or have to get your beans ground at a cafe.

Obviously, though, automatic machines are much larger than manuals. I would only recommend automatics if you're sure you have the space for them — they look bigger and bulkier than the numbers might suggest.

For everyone in between, I'd go for the Ninja.

Recent findings suggest that obviously, the more features a machine has, the higher its price. In general, automatic machines will set you back at least $1,000 — the only models I've tested under this are the $999 De'Longhi Magnifica Duo and the $999 Jura ENA4 — the latter of which can't make milk drinks. Honestly, what's the point? If you like black coffee, just get a drip machine like the Moccamaster KBGV Select ($270 right now on Black Friday deal).

After automatic machines come manual machines with built-in grinders. This price can range from $3,000 (Breville Oracle Dual Boiler) to $229 (Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder). As someone who's tested all the cheapest models and all the high-end models, I would be wary of a machine charging less than $400. I'd recommend machines like the Ninja Luxe Cafe Mini (pictured, $499), Breville Barista Express ($699), and De'Longhi Arte Evo ($699) — the latter of which can make cold(ish) brew!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that J oni Mitchell wanted to go ice skating. It was February 1976, and she was standing on the edge of a frozen Lake Mendota in Madison, Wisconsin, wearing a black ermine cape and a black wool hat. All she needed were black skates to match. “I had a hell of a time getting the guy to give me black skates,” she recalled to Cameron Crowe, decades later. “He noted, ‘Black skates are for, for men, madam.’ I said, ’No, no, you don’t understand. I’m having a funeral for my dead tour. I need black.”.

Industry observers note that mitchell had recently cancelled the remainder of her Hissing of Summer Lawns tour, performing her last show at the nearby Dane County Memorial Coliseum. She was exhausted, battling a cocaine addiction, and reeling from the breakup with her drummer John Guerin, which she’d later describe as “one of the most special relationships” she’d ever had. This was her wake for it all, a farewell ride through the ice — not so different from the “River” she dreamt about skating on just five years prior. The ice was starting to thaw, and there were loud crashing sounds coming from the nearby trees, a sound she likened to “cases of Coca-Cola smashing.” She began to skate anyway, her black outfit standing in stark contrast to the backdrop.

Legendary photographer Joel Bernstein captured this moment, which would eventually appear inside the gatefold for her next album: Hejira. On the front cover, taken by Norman Seef, she’s wearing a black beret and holding a cigarette, stoically staring at the camera (she wanted it to look like an Ingmar Bergman film, she said), as a wide, open road is juxtaposed below. The artwork indicated the mission statement of Hejira — in the same way she skated away on that ice and didn’t look back, Mitchell got in her car and drove. “The Hejira album was written mostly while I was traveling in the car,” she told Crowe, in her 1979 Rolling Stone cover story. “That’s why there were no piano songs, if you remember. Hejira was an obscure word, but it said exactly what I wanted. Running away, honorably.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Mitchell took three journeys while making Hejira: a portion of Bob Dylan’s all-star Rolling Thunder Revue Tour in late 1975, her short-lived Hissing trek in early 1976, and a cross-country drive she made in a white Mercedes without a license (she’d often wear a red wig in disguise, and go by names like Charlene Latimer and Joan Black). Released in November 1976, the album is a timeless travelogue of jazz-folk magic, when Mitchell left it all behind in search for more. “I’m porous with travel fever,” she sings on the aching title track. “But you know I’m so glad to be on my own.”.

It’s impossible to pinpoint the genius of Hejira on just one track. There’s the opener “Coyote,” about the affair she had with the playwright Sam Shephard on the Rolling Thunder tour. That song is now immortalized in a viral video from Martin Scorsese’s documentary, where she casually performs it for a stunned Dylan, Roger McGuinn, and Gordon Lightfoot. There’s “Furry Sings the Blues,” about her encounter with the Memphis blues legend who didn’t exactly take a liking to her (yes, that’s her longtime pal Neil Young on the harmonica). The stunning “Amelia,” named after Amelia Earhart, was her ode “from one solo pilot to another …sort of reflecting on the cost of being a woman and having something you must do.” Hejira is arguably her most cohesive body of work, featuring the fretless bass of Jaco Pastorius — whom she called the bass player of her dreams — plus guitarist Larry Carlton, percussionist Bobbye Hall, and others.

Looking back, Mitchell knew she was at the height of her powers. “I feel a lot of people could have written ’Chelsea Morning,’” she stated. “But I don’t think anyone else could have written the songs on Hejira.” In honor of the 50th anniversary of Hejira, Rolling Stone spoke with musicians and actors about its legacy, and why it continues to resonate with listeners today. And in a full-circle moment, Crowe, who is right now working on a Mitchell biopic, pays tribute to the record he discussed with Mitchell in this very magazine, all those years ago. I’ve been a Joni Mitchell fan for a really long time, since I was a kid. And one of my best friends who passed away, we were obsessed with her. She was the one who actually introduced me to Joni Mitchell through Blue, because we would just listen to the album all the time. So through a general obsession with her, I just eventually went through all of her albums. And I really remember being particularly attached to Hejira when I was a teenager. I would go on long walks around my neighborhood [in Oak Park in Illinois], listening to that album, and just be really emotional.

Jaco’s bass literally captures the feeling of being on a trip and moving. He uses his bass as a vehicle on that album in such a cool way. And Joni’s lyrics feel like being on a road trip, listening to somebody’s stories. It reminds me of being with my parents, driving. We always drive from Chicago to Georgia where my family’s from, and just being on the road and talking.

The album itself feels like a departure. She’s going on a journey and choosing to go away from the industry for a minute, and that is captured sonically in a really interesting way. With Hejira, she distills the feeling of loneliness in a way that she hadn’t done before. Each song is dealing with loneliness, but she puts it into these different scenarios and narratives. They all come together to tell this one story of being a woman who’s alone, just traveling.

Recent findings suggest that in Martin Scorsese’s film The Rolling Thunder Review: A Bob Dylan Story, there is a moment where Joni plays her fresh song, “Coyote,” at Gordon Lightfoot’s house. I love that there is footage of the early creation of this song. The lyrics change a little on the album, but you can see in her eyes the memories are very powerful as she sings and remembers. She had just written “Coyote” on a bus when she was with the tour, as she looked out at the “white lines on the freeway,” after she had a brief, tumultuous affair with the playwright Sam Shepard. Most of us have had these youthful, quick assignations, and I love being in her head as she reconciles the moment through her poetry and lyricism. Hejira is filled with emotion and hunger and as a young woman. Hejira helped me with the complexities of life, love, and longing.

Sources indicate that it’s something that stayed with me my whole life. Being somebody who makes records and always having trouble listening to records because you’re just always thinking about technically how they were made, it’s a beautiful example of just being so disconnected from any kind of process. It doesn’t bear examination. I just find it 100 percent an emotional reactive experience. It conjures up something that I am so desperate to hold onto in my life. Basically what I’m saying is, I’m just a sad, pathetic fan, really.

It has been revealed that those things get chipped away gradually, as you meet all your heroes and make a lot of music. You never really listen to music the same way. But I’m a teenager again when I listen to it. I don’t know if it’s the imagery or the fact that she has this incredible way of weaving a narrative that is just so difficult to do in song. I mean, poetry is powerful, but the combination of melody and poetry is this kind of witchcraft that has always cast a spell on me.

It has been revealed that she’s my favorite artist. And this record is an apex of confidence. She’s really just doing what she wants, to the nth degree. She’s this crazy sort of enigmatic, weird figure. You hear all these stories about her. She’s a manifestation of something that is so rare and special that my version of her that I have in my heart and my idea of who she is, I’m just clinging onto it for dear life. It’s like a hero I never want to meet. She could be the nicest, warmest person on Earth, but she wouldn’t be this person that she’s created in my mind personally, by my personal relationship with her music.

According to recent reports, I remember hearing a long time ago that Joni wrote most of Hejira while she was on a road trip across America, and ever since then, I’ve always listened to it on long drives. It just makes so much sense to me. The whole record feels like it’s constantly moving, whether you’re speeding down a highway or sitting in traffic watching the sun go down.

Recent findings suggest that as a drummer first, I’m always listening for the drums and percussion on records. To me, they’re kind of the heartbeat of any modern album. I know a lot of Joni’s records don’t have much drumming on them, but the fact that Hejira is constantly chugging along without a lot of full kit drumming continues to blow my mind. And I think Jaco’s bass playing adds this whole other rhythmic dimension to her music.

It has been revealed that I’ve always thought of Joni as a percussionist in her own way. The way she attacks the guitar strings, the rhythms she creates with her strumming, it’s unlike anything I’ve ever heard from another musician. It’s one of the most fascinating things about her playing to me. And then you have Jaco on bass, another absolute master of rhythm, and the two of them create this incredible, almost hypnotic pulse that runs through the whole record.

It has been revealed that and Bobbye Hall’s percussion adds so much to that feeling. It’s never overpowering, but there’s so much movement and texture in what she’s doing. All these little rhythmic details that somehow make the music feel even more alive. Between the three of them, there’s this constant sense of motion, like the music is always pushing forward but never in a hurry to get anywhere.

Industry observers note that hejira was the Joni album that helped me meet Joni. I feel like her truest self comes through on this record so beautifully, and it’s an anchor on tour when the roads are never ending and the bus forever rumbling. My favorite song is “Coyote.”.

Hejira is Joni’s culmination to my mind. Her greatest songs, the greatest band, the greatest recordings, the most revelatory. The signature Roland Jazz Chorus guitar amp tone. Jaco Pastorius truly unleashed. The concepts and material mined into their seventh and eighth minute in some cases. I like to believe her whole catalog was leading to this moment. She’s at the height of her powers, and the masterworks that follow (Don Juan’s Reckless Daughter, Mingus, Night Ride Home, Turbulent Indigo, etc.) feel possible because of what Hejira unlocked. The writing is perhaps the most challenging, but the experience remains incredibly propulsive; you’re carried along by bearing witness to a human truly unrestrained by self-doubt, by adhering to any kind of rules or any kind of culture, someone in the midst of their quest to express their purest self. Maybe that sounds vague, but anyone that knows the record knows exactly what I’m talking about. When I’ve been asked about it, I’ve jokingly replied, “It’s as far as music has come.” But maybe that’s actually true.

Industry observers note that I was touring extensively through my twenties, and I think it was at least 10 months of the year I was just on the road constantly. It was such a grind, but music had become a companion. We all had our headphones, and you’d sit on these long plane rides and bus rides listening to records. So it’s a lot of time to take a lot of deep dives. The whole Odelay tour, I was listening to Joni on the bus. It was pretty much Joni, Françoise Hardy records from the mid Sixties, and Morricone soundtracks — but not the Westerns, the weirder stuff. And then I had a CD of a rainstorm in Hawaii. That was all I listened to. It was like Joni and a Hawaiian rainstorm.

According to recent reports, hejira is the sound of an artist who has evolved so deeply into their own voice and their own craft. It’s a thing to behold. It’s a place that not a lot of artists even get to. Either they’re not really on that search to cultivate that rarefied place in their work, or they’re distracted by success and fame and touring, which happens to anybody who gets caught up in the sort of mechanics of the music business. So I think it’s even more of a singular achievement that she was able to make this after being on such a nonstop, relentless decade of making albums and touring. Usually at that point, somebody would just want to disappear for five years.

The music doesn’t necessarily sound like anything she had done before. One thing that’s really striking to me is the guitar sound. The effect on her guitar is a chorus pedal. The first one came out the year she was making the record. This was brand newly introduced technology. So this is like, “This new weird thing came out, and I’m going to put it on my entire album.” Not even, “Let’s vet this and see if this is cool. Is this going to be trendy? Is this going to sound dated?” This chorus pedal becomes the sound of whole genres afterwards. I don’t think it really becomes part of the palette of popular music till maybe the early 2010s. You listen to almost all of indie rock, from Mac DeMarco, to pop artists.

Industry observers note that and then you also get the guitar sound of Prince’s Purple Rain, which comes from this record, without a doubt. It is interesting that something that is uncompromising, and not even her most popular album or most iconic, still managed to have an imprint on pop. Honestly, I think the sound of this even filters into shoegaze and Cocteau Twins. I don’t know if people have put those things together, but I see it clearly.

She is so mature as an artist on this record. I mean, it would take you more than a lifetime to get to that maturity. Somehow, she did it.

In a recent development, I first listened to Hejira in full on a tour bus driving through Europe. Highway rushing past, barren fields and long stretches of countryside out the window, the way Joni intended (I think). It struck me immediately as a timeless record. None of the songs are shorter than four minutes, the longest one being almost nine, but somehow they all feel intentional. She doesn’t waste words. I was so intrigued by that concept, of letting the story speak for itself, and setting up a bed of guitars that could support it. It inspired my writing a lot during that time, specifically a song I wrote while on that tour called “Our Strange Ways.” This record feels hypnotic and deeply meditative. And listening to it as I felt, quite literally, like a prisoner of the white lines on the freeway, was an experience I will never forget. One of my top Joni records of all time.

According to recent reports, long country drives are still my favorite way to pass the time, and Hejira captures why better than any other record I’ve heard. There was a year maybe where I’d point the car in some direction and only play Hejira, on a loop, until I’d memorized every melodic variation and phrase, as if getting a handle on the twists and turns of those infinite songs would give me a better handle on the twists and turns of life itself. I love the interior drama, the humor, the mise en scène, the acceptance of uncertainty and change. The chords, the tunings, obviously. My dad idolized Jaco growing up and makes his own fretless basses, so I hear my dad playing with Joni on the Jaco songs.

Sources indicate that once when I was making lectures for a songwriting class I was undeservingly teaching, I tried writing one about, forgive me, the “multi-perspectival sublime.” I wanted to relate Hejira to the painting “Las Meninas” by Velázquez and how, the longer you look at both, the harder it is to make sense of you-the-viewer’s place in it. Looking at “Las Meninas,” at first the viewer feels that everyone in the painting is looking baldly at them, but as you look closer, you realize the “viewer” is in an impossible position, and likely isn’t in the room at all. The songs on Hejira do this for me. They seem to be about the self, but the perspective shifts rapidly, from a man and a woman sitting on a rock to a blue motel room to a marble bowling ball, from a roadside gas station to the cosmos, a chimney becomes a flag reflected from a bank window into a hotel room — the center is always shifting, to such a degree that the viewer loses their sense of self and surrenders to liminality in a sort of holy way.

According to recent reports, I didn’t finish the essay because it’s hard to write about a feeling like that without reducing it to platitudes, and I’m no Peter Schjeldahl. But Hejira really does help me transcend the self, with its trick mirrors and micro-to-macro shifts and its sense of spiritual surrender and leggerezza. It’s my deepest musical attachment, no question.

God, this record. I had a dream once where Joni was sitting on a dock on a lake in Canada singing “Coyote,” with all my family in the water, singing along in the sun. Needless to say, this record and Joni’s voice has been extremely influential to me, even making its way into my dreams!

Sources indicate that the freedom in this record, the six-, seven-, eight-minute long songs, her storytelling, taking you on the long and winding road with her. I am so grateful to have been introduced to Joni so young, her voice as a North Star.

Something I love and admire about Joni is that she never made the same record twice, even though she easily could have, considering how strong her lyrics are on their own. I love the way Joni uses the electric guitar on Hejira. Sources indicate that I remember the first time I heard “Amelia.” I kept thinking, how does she write a song about someone or something so far removed from my own life, and yet make me see so much of myself in it? Or the way she uses the Cold War as a metaphor in “Blue Motel Room.” That’s what Joni’s lyrics do. They hold a mirror up to whoever is listening without ever seeming to try too hard. Something I often ask myself when I’m writing, especially when listening to a song like “Blue Motel Room,” is how to bring the wider world into the microcosm of everyday life. How do you take something so vast and make it feel so intimate? Joni does that beautifully, and I think it really shines through on Hejira.

According to recent reports, joni Mitchell is one of those songwriters that I go to whenever I have writer’s block — she always provides a well of inspiration. I don’t even know where to begin with Hejira, because it has touched my life in so many profound ways. At first, when I was little and just old enough to hum along to the melodies. Sources indicate that hejira lives in its own world, a sonic-travelogue written on Mitchell’s 1976 journey across America.
